claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces resonant phonon-scattering centers that are more effective than the random-alloy scattering represented by a Debye-Callaway model.
MoNbTaW or NbMoTaW can form a chemically disordered, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Arc melting followed by high-temperature homogenization can ensure a random atomic distribution in the starting alloy.
Annealing at 0.4 to 0.6 of the melting temperature can induce significant SRO without causing long-range ordering or phase separation.
Rapid quenching can preserve the annealing-induced SRO state.
SRO produces specific nearest-neighbor pair correlations, such as Mo-W or Nb-Ta preferences.
These pair correlations create local potential-energy fluctuations distinct from the average lattice potential.
The local potential-energy fluctuations act as resonant scatterers for mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
Mass-variance and strain-field scattering dominate phonon transport in the chemically disordered state.
SRO creates local environments with vibrational densities of states distinct from those of the host lattice.
SRO-associated local vibrational modes resonate with propagating host-lattice phonons.
Resonant scattering significantly reduces phonon group velocity and phonon lifetime.
The reduction in phonon group velocity and lifetime lowers thermal conductivity below the random-alloy expectation.
An SRO-containing annealed sample will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the disordered sample throughout 300-1200 K.
The SRO-induced suppression will be strongest between 300 K and 800 K.
The strongest suppression occurs when phonon mean free paths are comparable to the SRO correlation length.
The proposed behavior is limited to single-phase BCC RHEAs with moderate-to-high atomic-size mismatch.
The hypothesis may not apply when SRO develops into a distinct long-range-ordered or phase-separated state.
The hypothesis may not apply when electronic thermal conductivity dominates, although such dominance is described as unlikely in refractory alloys.
